doctrine: VERIFIER_PIPELINE.md Stage-6: weight magnitudes in {5,3,1,0}; guardrails negative; narration <= 1; every weight carries weight_evidence; only deterministic criteria may gate.

criteria.criterion: OUTCOME CHANNEL. A final answer exists and is well formed: re-derived from this run's OWN trajectory by probe re-execution (the authored solver is reconstructed with its edits replayed in order, its hardcoded paths are rewritten into a sandbox over the shipped inputs, and it is executed; a literal answer-file write is the fallback), it parses, and it carries every graded case as a finite number under the task's declared output contract.
criteria.truth_ref: What a finished run must have produced
criteria.weight_evidence: Structural role: the outcome channel's shape check. Weight 3 (contract conformance, outcome-breaking): a correct calculation serialised outside the declared contract scores zero on the reward instrument. Route-independent - it grades the answer's shape, never how the answer was reached, and it is satisfied by a solver in any language or by a hand-written answer file. Not a nested duplicate of R2: the separating trajectory is the common one that emits a well-formed answer with a wrong value, which fails the tolerance criterion alone.

criteria.criterion: OUTCOME CHANNEL, GATE. Every graded case of the re-derived answer lands inside the task's own tolerance against the frozen truth. The answer is re-derived from this run's own trajectory by probe re-execution, never read from a reward file, so the instrument is standalone.
criteria.truth_ref: What a finished run must have produced
criteria.weight_evidence: GATE, weight 5: this is the outcome itself, and REQ-9 requires the wrong-answer gate (OUTCOME-FAILED) to cap final at 0.5 exactly as CRUX-FAILED does. The reference and the tolerance are the task's own frozen, control-measured values in verifier/expected_values.json - not a value invented for the rubric. Route-independent by construction: it reads only the answer, so every correct route satisfies it. Outcome mass is deliberately modest (8 of the rubric's total weight mass) - the channel's authority is the gate, not the mass.

Structural role: orientation precondition. A run that never opens instruments.json cannot key its output to the worksheet ids nor read the ICMA-only reference-period fields. Hygiene tier (weight 1) - low blast radius on its own, but every downstream step depends on it.

criteria.criterion: Authored a hand-written solver (a file, or an inline/heredoc python program) rather than relying on a finance library.
criteria.weight_evidence: Structural role: the task forbids day-count libraries and the runtime image lacks them, so a submission exists only if the run authored its own source. Hygiene tier (weight 1).

criteria.criterion: Executed python to compute the results and produce /root/results.json.
criteria.weight_evidence: Structural role: /root/results.json is produced by executing the solver; an authored-but-unexecuted program yields no submission for the outcome verifier to grade. Hygiene tier (weight 1).

criteria.criterion: Formed accrued interest as notional multiplied by annual_coupon_rate multiplied by the year fraction, for each instrument.
criteria.weight_evidence: Output-contract value: accrued_interest is the second graded quantity (accrued tolerance 1e-8). Omitting or mis-forming this product fails outcome test test_accrued_interest on all 11 instruments.

criteria.criterion: Applied the 30/360 US Bond Basis end-of-month cascade (last-day-of-February handling together with the 31->30 rule), not a plain 30/360.
criteria.weight_evidence: Measured control naive_30_360_no_eom_rules (control_gaps in expected_values.json): dropping the last-of-February + 31->30 cascade moves year_fraction far beyond the 1e-10 tolerance on the 30/360-US instruments (INST01-INST03), which include Feb-29 and 31st month-end stubs.

criteria.criterion: Applied the 30E/360 Eurobond rule (unconditional 31->30 on both endpoints with no February special case).
criteria.weight_evidence: Output-contract/tolerance: 30E/360 diverges from 30/360 US precisely on the 31st and end-of-February stubs present in the set (INST04-INST05); applying the wrong 30/360 variant fails test_year_fraction on those instruments at 1e-10.

criteria.criterion: Computed ACT/360 and ACT/365F with their distinct fixed denominators (360 versus 365), keeping the two apart.
criteria.weight_evidence: Measured control naive_360_for_365_mixup (control_gaps): using a 360 denominator for ACT/365F (or the reverse) moves year_fraction beyond the 1e-10 tolerance on the ACT/365F instrument (INST07).

criteria.criterion: Computed ACT/ACT ISDA by splitting the actual days across leap-year (366) and non-leap-year (365) segments, rather than dividing by a single denominator.
criteria.weight_evidence: Crux (TRUTH.md Step 6) plus two measured controls: naive_isda_as_365f and naive_actact_calendar_denom (control_gaps) both drive year_fraction orders of magnitude beyond tolerance on the ACT/ACT-ISDA instruments (INST08-INST09), which straddle year and leap boundaries. This is the recall the task isolates: the no-skill arm scored 0/5, the with-skill arm 5/5, so every recorded failure misses this rule - deterministic gate, precision ~1 for outcome failure.

criteria.criterion: Computed ACT/ACT ICMA with the period denominator coupon_frequency times the days in the reference coupon period, not a calendar-year 365/366.
criteria.weight_evidence: Crux (TRUTH.md Step 7) plus measured control naive_actact_calendar_denom (control_gaps): an ICMA period computed with a calendar-year 365/366 denominator instead of coupon_frequency times reference-period days misses the 1e-10 tolerance on the ICMA instruments (INST10-INST11), where short quarterly vs long semiannual periods widen the gap. Human twin carries weight but only this deterministic criterion gates.

criteria.criterion: Emitted /root/results.json under the results contract, keyed by instrument id with year_fraction and accrued_interest.
criteria.weight_evidence: Structural role: output-contract shape. A malformed shape fails the outcome fixture (res) before any tolerance check runs. Hygiene tier (weight 1) - shape, not rule.

criteria.criterion: GUARDRAIL: the run applied a single uniform day-count formula to every instrument (for example actual-days/365 or actual-days/360 throughout), doing no per-convention dispatch.
criteria.weight_evidence: Measured control naive_days_over_365 (control_gaps): a uniform actual-days/365 (or /360) formula is the dominant no-skill failure and the largest tabulated gap in the ledger. Firing means the run did no per-convention work. Behavioural/grading-integrity guardrail, negative magnitude 3 mirrors the positive convention tier.

criteria.criterion: GUARDRAIL: the run imported a forbidden finance or day-count library (QuantLib, financepy, isda, python-dateutil day-count helpers, or pandas offset utilities).
criteria.weight_evidence: Grading-integrity: task.md Forbidden clause bans these libraries; importing one bypasses the recall-and-hand-implement capability the paired skill measurement is built to isolate, so a passing outcome would not reflect the skill. Negative magnitude 3.

criteria.criterion: The run forms three genuinely different denominators for ACT/ACT ISDA, ACT/ACT ICMA and ACT/365F, and the trajectory shows what each one is built out of: for ISDA the actual days are split by the calendar year they fall in and each part divided by that year's own length and summed, not divided by a single year's denominator; for ICMA the denominator is the coupon frequency multiplied by the length of the supplied reference coupon period; for ACT/365F it is a fixed 365. Dispatching on the basis name, or stating that the Actual/Actual conventions differ, does not satisfy this on its own - each of the three denominators has to be visible as a different quantity in the run's own construction or arithmetic.
criteria.weight_evidence: Behavioural human twin of the two ACT/ACT crux criteria: the discrimination-matrix rows naive_isda_as_365f and naive_actact_calendar_denom are precisely these confusions. Weight 3 (behavioural, work product = differential application); human-reviewed, so it carries no gate flag - reviewer disagreement disqualifies a human-reviewed gate. REVISED 2026-08-19 (degenerate-criterion remediation): the shipped text asked whether the reasoning APPLIES three denominators, which any per-basis dispatch satisfies, and it returned the same verdict on all twelve pinned runs of this bundle. The text now asks what each denominator is BUILT OUT OF - the per-calendar-year split for ISDA (TRUTH.md Step 6), coupon frequency times the supplied reference period for ICMA (Step 7), the fixed 365 for ACT/365F (Step 5) - which is the same work product, differential application, stated at the granularity the two discrimination-matrix rows actually separate. Weight unchanged at 3; still human-reviewed, still no gate flag. DEMOTED TO WEIGHT 0, 2026-08-19 (recorded demoting finding, degenerate-criterion remediation, second pass): after the 2026-08-19 revision the criterion still returned satisfied on all twelve pinned-cohort runs, and the reason is structural on this sample - every one of the twelve passes the deterministic twins of the same competence (R10, the ACT/ACT ISDA leap-split gate, and R11, the ICMA period denominator, weight 5), so the cohort holds no weak case on this dimension for a human twin to separate; mass spent here is mass no verdict can move. The criterion is correctly scoped and its verdicts remain recorded report-only; restore a scored weight only when a cohort shows a separating case (a run that dispatches on basis names while passing neither deterministic twin).

criteria.criterion: The run verifies a result against something that could disagree - a hand-recomputed day count, a cross-convention difference on shared dates, or a leap-boundary spot check - not merely by re-running its own solver.
criteria.weight_evidence: Behavioural with a work product: this is the Stage-7 verification move mapped to TRUTH.md Step 9's discrimination table. Re-running one's own solver cannot catch a convention slip; a check that can disagree can. Weight 3.

criteria.criterion: The reasoning engages the pull toward naive calendar-day arithmetic (a single 365/360 denominator) and sets it aside in favour of the per-convention ISDA rules.
criteria.weight_evidence: Narration-adjacent recognition (the channel's structural proxy gap): engaging the naive-default temptation is read from prose and only weakly evidences the work. Capped at weight 1 by the narration doctrine.

mece: REQ-9: the criterion set is MECE across the outcome and process instruments jointly. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE - no two criteria are decided by the same evidence; for every pair there is a trajectory that fails exactly one, argued in each criterion's weight_evidence. The deliberate exception is a d_ criterion and its human twin on the same subject: they rest on different evidence (what the code did vs. what the reasoning earned) and are separable in both directions. COLLECTIVELY EXHAUSTIVE - see the `coverage` block. THREE CHANNELS - `outcome` (o_*: pytest that re-derives the final answer by probe re-execution of the run's own solver), `deterministic` (d_*: mechanics over the trajectory), `human` (n_*: the human-reviewed rubric) - blended by weight mass with TWO gates capping identically at 0.5: CRUX-FAILED and OUTCOME-FAILED.

mutual_exclusivity_review.note: VERIFIER_PIPELINE Stage 2 rule 7 audit, corroborated by _qc/criterion_independence.py. Operative test: can a run fail exactly one of the two criteria? Nothing was deleted - a criterion that loses weight keeps its row and its detector so the firing table still records it.
instrument_findings: FIXTURE SUITE NOT ISOLATING: 11 of 13 fixtures trip more than 60 percent of the rubric. Every NEGATIVE / planted-defect fixture in this bundle is a terse snippet that trips most of the rubric rather than isolating one defect - _qc/criterion_independence.py reports the suite as NOT ISOLATING - so criteria with entirely unrelated predicates come out with identical columns. The duplication is in the SUITE, not in the weights, and the work item is a fixture per criterion that leaves everything else plausible. Until that is fixed the empirical arm of rule 7 cannot certify this bundle either way, and the six-way identical column below must not be read as six duplicated criteria.

pairs.shape: identical columns over the shipped fixtures
pairs.verdict: ARTIFACT of a non-isolating suite, no weight change
pairs.separating_trajectory: Exists for every pair and is trivial to state: a solver that implements 30E/360 correctly and splits the ACT/ACT ISDA year at the leap boundary wrongly fails exactly one of the first and fourth. The predicates read different bytes - an end-of-month clamp, a 30/360 numerator, a leap-year split, a period denominator, two distinct day bases, a contract key - and share no expression. What no SHIPPED FIXTURE does is exercise one of them while leaving the rest plausible.
pairs.action: none to the weights. Demoting a correctly-scoped criterion because the fixture suite is coarse would remove real measurement to make a QC report clean.

pairs.separating_trajectory: One fixture fails R10 and the other conventions while R13 stays quiet - the run branches per convention and gets a branch wrong, which is not the uniform-naive route. The guardrail fires only when NO convention dimension enters the run at all, which is the severest degree and a separate question under rule 7.
pairs.action: none. Its magnitude (3) is already one tier below the gate (5) it shadows, which is the rule applied across this dataset.

pairs.separating_trajectory: The commonest trajectory on any of these tasks: a well-formed answer carrying every graded case as a finite number, with a wrong value. The shape check passes and the tolerance gate fails.

No d_ criterion in this bundle reads a graded VALUE - every one reads the route. A hand-transcribed correct answer satisfies the outcome gate and fails R4 / R5; a run on the blessed route can still miss tolerance through an arithmetic slip.

coverage.note: REQ-9 collective exhaustiveness / VERIFIER_PIPELINE Stage 2 rule 8: every TRUTH.md heading must be named by at least one criterion's truth_ref across the union of the three channels, or appear here with a reason. Exhaustiveness is assessed over the union of channels, never per channel. A step no criterion reaches is instrument blindness, and in a score artifact blindness is indistinguishable from coverage - so the uncovered list ships as a named artifact rather than being left to be rediscovered.
